channel.title: English — UpahJe.my
channel.description: Plain, sourced answers about technology for Malaysian small businesses.

item.title: CommandCode, OpenCode, DeepSeek: three names, three different things
item.description: One is a paid CLI, one is a free CLI, one is an API. Their published prices, their drift, and one run that shows an exit code of zero is not success.

item.title: Google Business Profile: the fields that decide whether you show up
item.description: Google documents the name rules, the category rules, hours, service areas and what triggers suspension. What an SME should fix first, and the four fields that get profiles restricted.

item.title: Where the same data gets typed three times
item.description: Malaysian adoption is not the problem: 97.2% of establishments use computers. The duplication sits between a digitised front office and a manual back office, and e-Invoice now forces one record to be right at issuance.

item.title: What an AI agent can and cannot do for a Malaysian SME
item.description: An AI agent runs a loop on its own: it reads a task, calls tools, checks the result and repeats. What that covers unattended, what needs a human signature, and what no agent should touch.

item.title: Your first automation should not be your worst process
item.description: Opinion. The process an owner hates most is usually the worst one to automate first, because automating it removes the evidence you need and hides the exceptions that decide the cost.

item.title: Agent harness, AI harness, agent framework: what the words mean
item.description: An agent harness runs the agent loop: it executes tool calls, holds the transcript, applies permissions. Vendors say agent harness. AI harness is not a term they use. A table of who says what.

item.title: Agent harnesses ranked: four CLIs installed on one machine
item.description: DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode installed on one machine, scored 1-5 on five weighted criteria using only what we could read from each on 19 November 2026.

item.title: What automation work costs in Malaysia: published rates, six sources
item.description: Four Malaysian studios, one independent practitioner and one freelance profile: 30 published prices for automation and integration work, checked 19 November 2026 except one page read on 27 October 2026. Several source pages carry no publication date, so a price may be older than this article.

item.title: Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok: what actually differs between the closed models
item.description: Not the benchmark score, which no current leaderboard here can settle. What you are stuck with: context window, price per token and the documented capabilities. Every cell sourced or marked not captured, and where the terms pages were not opened, the article says so.

item.title: Do you need an API, or just a spreadsheet?
item.description: A spreadsheet wins at low volume with one owner; an API wins when two systems must stay in sync without anyone copying. The three cases where a sheet is right, and the four signals it has stopped scaling.

item.title: Where your API key goes in a harness, and where it must never go
item.description: A harness reads your key from an environment variable or its credential store when it calls the provider. What the key authenticates, the four places it must never appear, and what to do when it leaks.

item.title: Agent harnesses: who makes them, and what is actually open source
item.description: Grok Bot and Dots are closed hosted products. OpenBot and MausBot are source-available projects, and only one of them is open source on its own licence. A table with the licence and the evidence level on every row.

item.title: How to brief an automation job so you don't pay twice
item.description: Five things a freelancer needs before quoting, a reusable brief template, and the acceptance test to agree before work starts. Written for a Malaysian SME buying automation for the first time.

item.title: Open-weight models: Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral and Kimi, and what the licence lets you do
item.description: Four open-weight families, five model cards, four licence shapes. MIT on DeepSeek, a custom Qwen licence, Mistral's own open-weight licence. What each permits and what the model costs to rent.

item.title: Open or closed models: what a Malaysian SME can actually run in-house
item.description: An open-weight model can be downloaded and run on hardware you control. What that costs per month in Malaysia, the volume where it beats paying per call, and the skills it needs.

item.title: What RM100 a month buys you in AI, in Malaysia
item.description: RM100 is either a seat in a subscription app or a meter of API tokens, never both. The conversion at Bank Negara's 19 November 2026 rate, three worked usage levels, and the line where tokens win.

item.title: Five side-income skills in Malaysia that actually pay in 2026
item.description: Five skills clear a two-listing bar on the one Malaysian freelance platform whose public pages could be read: video editing, graphic design, data entry, cold calling and app testing. Rates, counts and dates from 11 listings.

item.title: What an agent harness is, and what it does with your request
item.description: A harness sits between you and the model: it holds the conversation, runs the tools, sends each request and streams the answer. What one message looks like inside DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.1.

item.title: What is an API, explained for a Malaysian small business owner
item.description: An API is a contract that lets two systems exchange data without a human copying it across. What it means for a Malaysian SME, open versus closed models, and the real cost of wiring one up.
